doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Future plans and Milt Hinton's late debut as leader
summary: He hopes to do more; Hinton got his first major-label date at 85.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Yeah. Well the state of jazz for you is pretty productive I think for the most part.
The state of jazz for me?
Your involvement in jazz seems to be in a fairly healthy state. Can I say that?

Yeah. I like that idea. I’m in agreement with that idea. I have all sorts of delusions of grandeur and I’d like to take it a whole lot farther than I have, but the album I’m about to © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -23-

give you some time before I leave will at least give you a hint, a very slight hint of one of the ways I’d like to take it. But I need some kind of firmer foundation beneath me to be able to do something like that, like a very rich backer type of person.
Well if we use Milt Hinton for a judge, you have another forty years or so where you can—
Can you believe that he was 85 when he had his first record out under his own name on a major label?

85 before Columbia gave him a date. Now that’s one way to look at that. You could look at it as he made a zillion other records, but he neither asked nor planned on being the leader, so it’s all how you look at it I guess. I’m sure he doesn’t have any complaints.
